rationale: A defensible leg-swap that recombines the archive's two best-performing quality channels, but it is an incremental permutation of BuybackVerifiedCheapness whose dominant leg remains the published net-share-issuance effect, and the claim of "no shared denominator" is only partly true since turnover change and working-capital change both key off the same (act−che) stock.

This is BuybackVerifiedCheapness with the issuance horizon changed from one to three years — a single-parameter cosmetic variant that also moves the signal closer to the well-documented multi-year net-share-issuance anomaly rather than testing a new economic mechanism.

Adding the turnover-level leg to the winning composite is a legitimate test of whether verification is multi-dimensional, but the nested SUMRANK silently assigns the buyback leg twice the weight of each operating leg, contradicting the stated rationale that "no leg dominates," and the design risks diluting the parent rather than sharpening it.

Upgrading the value anchor while holding the quality composite fixed is a clean, previously untested design isolation, though the hard-book numerator partially double-counts the working-capital-release leg (level versus change of the same construct) and its parent's alpha evidence was weak.

This is the most informative proposal in the set — a genuine falsification test distinguishing a general cash-verification mechanism from the published equity-issuance effect — though GROWTH on total debt is unstable or undefined for low- and zero-debt firms and may mechanically load on leverage/distress rather than cash generation.

Two prior MIN-screen constructions in the archive already produced the same diagnostic pattern (large FMB slopes with null or negative FF5 alpha), so a third instance is a structural retread whose likely outcome — nonlinearity inflating the cross-sectional slope without tradable alpha — is already established.
